newsitem.title: USA: Sun offers Chateau cash in $390 million bid.
newsitem.headline: Sun offers Chateau cash in $390 million bid.

text.p: Sun Communities Inc. fought back Wednesday in the takeover battle for mobile home park operator Chateau Properties Inc., offering a cash alternative to its existing stock-swap merger proposal valued at about $390 million.
Sun's cash offer for Chateau, however, appeared to fall shy of a $400 million takeover bid from Chicago property developer Sam Zell's Manufactured Home Communities Inc.
Chateau, which manages communities made up of manufactured homes in the Midwest and Southeast, has already signed a definitive agreement to merge with another real estate trust, ROC Communities Inc.
All four companies operate sites for pre-fabricated homes.

"We are flexible with respect to both the structure of the combination and the type of consideration offered," Sun said in a letter to Chateau's board of directors. "We are prepared to provide a cash alternative to the extent desired by your shareholders."

Sun previously offered Chateau shareholders 0.892 shares of Sun Communities, which also has properties in the Midwest and Southeast, for each share of Clinton Township, Mich.-based Chateau's common stock.

Chateau said last week it continued to consider unsolicited takeover proposals, and also noted that its articles of incorporation prohibited a person or entity from owning more than 7 percent of the firm's outstanding common stock without board approval.
Chateau, which manages communities made up of manufactured homes in the Midwest and Southeast, said last week it was continuing to consider unsolicited takeover proposals.
Chateau stock closed up 62.5 cents at $26.75 on the New York Stock Exchange. Sun Communities closed down 12.5 cents at $28.875 on the NYSE.
